source_concept: Define and maintain security requirements for the development process, internally developed software, and third-party components.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe how security requirements enter development work and how they are communicated across internal and supplier boundaries.
illustrative_evidence: Documented development requirements; secure-development standards; supplier requirements; sampled backlog or acceptance criteria.
adaptation_limit: SSDF describes high-level secure-development practices and outcomes; this row does not establish a maturity level or prove implementation.

source_concept: Define and communicate roles and responsibilities for secure software development.
proposed_assessment_use: Assess clarity of ownership, review accountability, and escalation paths across development participants.
illustrative_evidence: RACI or role descriptions; review assignments; onboarding/training material; interview corroboration.
adaptation_limit: Role documentation alone is evidence of design intent, not operating effectiveness.

source_concept: Configure tools to generate artifacts and evidence that support secure development and continuous improvement.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether toolchains produce traceable evidence for build, review, test, and release decisions.
illustrative_evidence: CI/CD logs; code-review records; test reports; dependency outputs; artifact provenance records.
adaptation_limit: SSDF does not require a particular toolchain or vendor and does not by itself define a validated maturity scale.

source_concept: Define criteria for software security checks and track them through the SDLC.
proposed_assessment_use: Examine whether review/test gates have explicit criteria, exceptions, and traceable completion evidence.
illustrative_evidence: Definition-of-done language; gate criteria; exception records; KPI/KRI definitions; sampled releases.
adaptation_limit: Locally proposed assessment criteria must be distinguished from the SSDF source language.

source_concept: Review software design against security requirements and risk information.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe design-review timing, independence, evidence, and treatment of security-relevant design decisions.
illustrative_evidence: Architecture/design reviews; threat or risk analyses; approval comments; remediation follow-through.
adaptation_limit: A design-review artifact does not demonstrate code quality or production effectiveness without corroborating evidence.

source_concept: Follow secure coding practices appropriate to the programming language and environment.
proposed_assessment_use: Examine how secure coding expectations are defined, taught, reviewed, and sampled across teams.
illustrative_evidence: Coding standards; review checklists; static-analysis configuration; sampled review comments; developer interviews.
adaptation_limit: SSDF is technology-neutral; this mapping does not prescribe a language, scanner, or coding standard.

source_concept: Use current build tools and approved, controlled build configurations to improve executable security.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe reproducibility, approved build configuration, change control, and integrity of build environments.
illustrative_evidence: Build definitions; runner configuration; version pinning; change history; reproducibility evidence.
adaptation_limit: A controlled build process is one component of secure delivery and is not a complete maturity determination.

source_concept: Risk-management strategy outcomes cover objectives, appetite/tolerance, enterprise integration, response options, communication, and standardized risk methods.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether cybersecurity risk decisions are explicit, repeatable, connected to enterprise priorities, and understood by service owners.
illustrative_evidence: Risk criteria; escalation thresholds; risk registers; governance minutes; documented acceptance or treatment decisions.
adaptation_limit: CSF Core outcomes are non-prescriptive; this mapping does not certify compliance or assign a maturity score.

source_concept: Roles, responsibilities, authorities, and accountability for cybersecurity risk management are established and communicated.
proposed_assessment_use: Examine decision rights and operational accountability across central IT, service teams, security, and partners.
illustrative_evidence: Organization charts; role descriptions; governance charters; incident roles; sampled decision records.
adaptation_limit: Formal ownership is not equivalent to demonstrated execution; corroborate with observed records and interviews.

source_concept: Identity management, authentication, and access-control outcomes limit access to authorized users, services, and hardware commensurate with risk.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe identity lifecycle, authentication, authorization, federation, privileged access, and evidence of periodic governance.
illustrative_evidence: Access-control standards; IAM workflows; sampled joiner/mover/leaver cases; MFA/federation configuration evidence; review records.
adaptation_limit: Category-level use guides discovery; it does not assume a specific Iowa IAM architecture or product.

source_concept: Data-security outcomes address protection of data consistent with risk strategy.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe data handling, protection, integrity, retention, and transfer controls in the assessed service context.
illustrative_evidence: Data-flow diagrams; classification/handling rules; encryption configuration; retention evidence; sampled exceptions.
adaptation_limit: Applicability depends on system data and legal/policy context; public policy cannot prove operational practice.

source_concept: Continuous-monitoring outcomes cover observation of assets and activity for adverse cybersecurity events.
proposed_assessment_use: Examine coverage, ownership, alert routing, tuning, evidence retention, and linkage from detection to response.
illustrative_evidence: Monitoring inventories; alert rules; sampled alerts/incidents; coverage maps; review/tuning history.
adaptation_limit: Monitoring-tool presence alone does not establish detection effectiveness or maturity.

source_concept: Incident response outcomes address management, analysis, and mitigation of cybersecurity incidents.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe incident intake, severity, coordination, analysis, containment/mitigation, decision records, and learning.
illustrative_evidence: Incident procedures; sampled tickets/timelines; post-incident reviews; escalation records; corrective actions.
adaptation_limit: Incident examples are context-specific and should not be generalized without period, scope, and denominator.

source_concept: Secure and harden development endpoints and environments, including access controls and monitoring appropriate to risk.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe protection of development environments and administrative paths that can affect software integrity.
illustrative_evidence: Endpoint hardening standards; privileged-access evidence; MFA configuration; monitoring coverage; sampled exceptions.
adaptation_limit: The source targets secure development environments; it should not be stretched into an enterprise-wide control certification.

source_concept: Prefer standardized security features and services for capabilities such as logging, identity, access control, and vulnerability management.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether teams reuse governed security services instead of repeatedly creating bespoke security mechanisms.
illustrative_evidence: Reference architectures; shared-service catalogs; adoption records; approved exception patterns; developer interviews.
adaptation_limit: Reuse is context-sensitive; this mapping is not a procurement recommendation and does not prescribe a vendor.

source_concept: Technology-infrastructure resilience outcomes address protection of availability and resilience consistent with risk strategy.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe resiliency design, dependency management, capacity, failover, and recovery assumptions for assessed services.
illustrative_evidence: Architecture diagrams; redundancy/failover evidence; dependency maps; resilience tests; service objectives.
adaptation_limit: CSF outcomes do not establish a universal uptime target or peer benchmark.

source_concept: Continuous monitoring and adverse-event analysis outcomes connect observation to event characterization.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe observability coverage, alert-to-event workflow, triage quality, and whether operational evidence can be traced to decisions.
illustrative_evidence: Telemetry/alert inventories; event records; triage procedures; sampled alerts; analysis notes.
adaptation_limit: Availability of telemetry is not equivalent to useful coverage; effectiveness requires contextual evidence.

source_concept: Response-management, communication, and mitigation outcomes support coordinated handling of incidents.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe operational incident ownership, communications, mitigation authority, and cross-service coordination.
illustrative_evidence: Runbooks; on-call/escalation records; incident communications; mitigation timelines; post-incident actions.
adaptation_limit: Assessment should separate cybersecurity incident response from broader service-management practices where evidence differs.

source_concept: Recovery-plan execution and recovery communication outcomes support restoration after incidents.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe recovery procedures, restoration priorities, testing, stakeholder communication, and evidence of lessons carried forward.
illustrative_evidence: Recovery plans; exercise/test records; restore evidence; communications; corrective-action tracking.
adaptation_limit: Recovery outcomes do not prescribe a single disaster-recovery architecture or target recovery objective.

source_concept: Improvement outcomes use evaluations, tests, exercises, and operational experience to improve cybersecurity risk management.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether incidents, exercises, service reviews, and assessment findings reliably become owned improvements.
illustrative_evidence: Retrospectives; problem records; action registers; change records; closure evidence; trend reviews.
adaptation_limit: Improvement evidence should be sampled over a defined period; isolated retrospectives do not establish sustained practice.

source_concept: Toolchains should generate artifacts and evidence supporting secure development and continuous improvement.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether deployment pipelines produce inspectable records that support release traceability and learning.
illustrative_evidence: Pipeline logs; signed/traceable artifacts; approvals; deployment records; rollback records.
adaptation_limit: This is a secure-development reference; operational reliability conclusions require separate service evidence.

source_concept: Approved configurations and controlled build environments support executable security.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe promotion/build controls, environment drift, privileged changes, and reproducibility at the build-to-release boundary.
illustrative_evidence: Environment definitions; build/deploy configuration; change-control records; sampled releases.
adaptation_limit: Do not infer broader environment-management maturity solely from build controls.

source_concept: Plan monitoring and periodic review, maintain an AI-system inventory, and provide safe decommissioning processes.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether AI use is inventoried, periodically reviewed, monitored, and retired through explicit ownership and criteria.
illustrative_evidence: AI inventory; review cadence; system owners; monitoring plans; retirement/decommission records.
adaptation_limit: AI RMF actions are not a checklist and are not a validated maturity scale; AI RMF 1.0 is being revised.

source_concept: Establish AI-risk roles, lines of communication, training, and executive responsibility.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe accountability and enablement for AI-related development/use across technical, risk, legal/policy, and leadership participants.
illustrative_evidence: Role definitions; governance charter; training records; escalation paths; leadership review evidence.
adaptation_limit: Governance structure should be adapted to local size and context; the source does not prescribe an organization chart.

source_concept: Document intended purpose, context, business value, risk tolerance, and requirements from relevant AI actors.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether AI-enabled work begins with a documented purpose, affected users, operating context, limits, and risk/benefit rationale.
illustrative_evidence: Use-case records; architecture/context documents; stakeholder requirements; data/use constraints; risk assumptions.
adaptation_limit: This does not imply that every automation is an AI system; define the assessment population before applying the mapping.

source_concept: Select risk metrics, document what cannot be measured, reassess metric/control appropriateness, and involve independent or non-front-line perspectives where needed.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe whether AI evaluation has defined measures, explicit limitations, review independence, and a path to update measures as risks change.
illustrative_evidence: Evaluation plans; metric definitions; error/impact reporting; independent review evidence; documented unmeasurable risks.
adaptation_limit: Metrics must fit the use case and population; the mapping does not supply empirical thresholds or peer percentiles.

source_concept: Document TEVV test sets, metrics, and tools; evaluate under deployment-like conditions; monitor behavior in production.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe pre-deployment evaluation traceability, representativeness of test conditions, and post-deployment monitoring.
illustrative_evidence: Test/evaluation records; test-set provenance; acceptance criteria; production monitoring; drift/performance review.
adaptation_limit: Observed measures should be interpreted within their stated conditions; this row does not endorse any universal AI benchmark.

source_concept: Make proceed/no-proceed decisions, prioritize treatment, document responses, and document residual risk.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe decision gates, treatment ownership, residual-risk acceptance, and traceability from evaluation to deployment decision.
illustrative_evidence: Risk-treatment plans; gate decisions; exception/acceptance records; residual-risk statements; approval history.
adaptation_limit: A locally designed go/no-go threshold is not a NIST-required threshold; distinguish organization decisions from source guidance.

source_concept: Respond and recover when previously unknown AI risks emerge; disengage or deactivate systems whose outcomes are inconsistent with intended use.
proposed_assessment_use: Probe AI incident response, override/disable authority, fallback paths, and retirement triggers.
illustrative_evidence: Incident/issue records; rollback or disable procedures; fallback design; owner decisions; communications.
adaptation_limit: Applicability depends on actual AI-enabled services and their impact; hypothetical capability is not evidence of readiness.

section_or_id: Profile-wide; use only for in-scope generative-AI use cases
source_concept: Companion profile tailors AI RMF considerations to generative-AI risks and actions.
proposed_assessment_use: Use as a conditional drill-down when discovery confirms generative-AI development, integration, or operational use.
illustrative_evidence: GenAI use-case inventory; model/provider documentation; content/data handling; evaluation and monitoring artifacts.
adaptation_limit: Do not use as the baseline for all AI; it is a generative-AI companion profile, not evidence that Iowa uses generative AI.

section_or_id: Profile-wide; augment SP 800-218 for GenAI and dual-use foundation-model development
source_concept: Augments SSDF 1.1 with practices specific to generative-AI and dual-use foundation-model development.
proposed_assessment_use: Use only if assessed teams develop or materially modify models within the publication's scope; otherwise retain SSDF 1.1 as the software baseline.
illustrative_evidence: Model-development lifecycle records; model/data provenance; model-specific testing; release and monitoring evidence.
adaptation_limit: Do not generalize this model-development profile to ordinary use of third-party AI features or non-model software development.
